Case_08011/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1. Biopsy of the epiglottis, PAS stain, high magnification.

description.short_caption: PAS-stained biopsy of the epiglottis showing fungal elements.
description.detailed_description: This high-magnification histopathology image shows a biopsy of the epiglottis stained with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS). The image reveals numerous fungal elements, including yeast forms and pseudohyphae, which are stained magenta against a pink and purple background. The cellular architecture is disrupted, with inflammatory cells and necrotic debris visible. The PAS stain highlights the polysaccharide-rich fungal cell walls.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive bacilli in chains.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of bacterial culture growth. Numerous gram-positive bacilli are visible, arranged in chains and scattered across the field. The organisms are stained purple, consistent with their gram-positive nature, against a clear background. The morphology and arrangement suggest a specific bacterial species, but further identification would require additional testing.

Case_08011/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Bacilli on biopsy specimen (see arrow), PAS stain.

description.short_caption: PAS stain showing bacilli on tissue biopsy (arrow).
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a tissue section stained with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain. The stain highlights intracellular and extracellular structures, with a focus on bacilli indicated by the arrow. The bacilli appear as rod-shaped organisms with a magenta hue against a lighter background. The surrounding tissue shows cellular and extracellular matrix components, with some areas of amorphous material.
visible_findings: PAS stain highlighting organisms and tissue structures
background of cellular and extracellular tissue components

Case_08011/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Growth from biopsy specimen on sheep blood agar.

description.short_caption: Bacterial growth on sheep blood agar from a biopsy specimen.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a culture plate with sheep blood agar displaying bacterial growth. The colonies are white, opaque, and exhibit a spreading pattern. The agar appears red, consistent with the blood agar medium. No hemolysis is visibly apparent around the colonies, suggesting non-hemolytic bacteria. The streaking pattern indicates isolation of colonies for identification.
visible_findings: red background of sheep blood agar
